factual_claims.claim: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) improves the factual accuracy and domain coverage of Large Language Models (LLMs) by integrating external retrieval mechanisms.
Basic RAG systems struggle with real-world, industrial-scale applications involving complex and heterogeneous data, often producing fragmented or contradictory responses.
Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) like OpenAI's o1 and DeepSeek-R1 are developed using large-scale reinforcement learning to excel at complex, multi-step reasoning tasks.
LLMs with long context windows suffer from a 'lost-in-the-middle' phenomenon where information in the middle of the input is less effectively processed than information at the beginning or end.
DeepRetrieval uses reinforcement learning (PPO) to train an LLM to rewrite user queries for better retrieval performance, using recall and NDCG as reward signals.
ReZero improves agentic search by incentivizing persistence, rewarding the agent for issuing additional search queries when the initial attempt fails.
Large language models exhibit a persistent and quantifiable phenomenon of hallucination, which researchers are actively working to define and remediate.
